CVE-2026-48962 is a CWE-95 eval sink in File::GlobMapper (IO::Compress, perl-modules-5.40) reachable via an attacker-controlled output glob. The datahub-ingestion -dev variants install only perl-base; perl-modules-5.40 is not installed and File::GlobMapper is absent from disk. The vulnerable code is not shipped; the scanner flags it via perl-base sharing the `perl` source package.

CVE-2026-48959 is a DoS in the IO::Uncompress::Unzip perl module, which ships in the perl-modules-5.40 binary package. The datahub-ingestion -dev variants install only perl-base; perl-modules-5.40 is not installed and the module is absent from disk. The vulnerable code is not shipped; the scanner flags it via perl-base sharing the `perl` source package.

CVE-2026-42497 is in the Archive::Tar perl module (perl-modules-5.40). The datahub-ingestion -dev variants install only perl-base; perl-modules-5.40 is not installed and Archive::Tar is absent from disk. The vulnerable code is not shipped; the scanner flags it via perl-base sharing the `perl` source package.

CVE-2026-9538 is a memory-exhaustion DoS in the Archive::Tar perl module (perl-modules-5.40). The datahub-ingestion -dev variants install only perl-base; perl-modules-5.40 is not installed and Archive::Tar is absent from disk. CVE-2026-42496 is a symlink path-traversal in the Archive::Tar perl module, which ships in the perl-modules-5.40 binary package. The datahub-ingestion -dev variants install only perl-base (5.40.1-6); perl-modules-5.40 is not installed and the module is absent from disk (`perl -MArchive::Tar -e1` fails to locate it). The scanner attributes the CVE to the shared `perl` source package via the installed perl-base, but the vulnerable code is not shipped in this image.

CVE-2026-7010 is a CRLF injection in the HTTP::Tiny perl module (request line, Host header, and HTTP/1.1 control field values; fixed upstream in HTTP::Tiny 0.093, unfixed in trixie). The scanner attributes it to the shared perl source package via the installed perl-base, but HTTP::Tiny ships in perl-modules-5.40, which this image does not install: the datahub-ingestion -dev variants carry only perl-base 5.40.1-6 (a git dependency). Verified in the built image: no HTTP/Tiny.pm exists on the filesystem and `perl -MHTTP::Tiny -e 1` fails with "Can't locate HTTP/Tiny.pm in @INC", so the vulnerable code is not present.

CVE-2010-0928 is the 2010 RSA-CRT fault-injection attack (Pellegrini et al.): recovering a private key requires physically inducing computational faults (voltage/clock manipulation) in the CPU while it performs RSA operations. There is no remote or local-software attack vector; OpenSSL upstream disputes the issue (fault injection is outside its threat model per the OpenSSL security policy) and Debian has marked it unimportant with no fix planned since 2010. A container boundary offers no surface for hardware fault injection beyond what the host already implies. In datahub-ingestion the non-fips variants install the Debian openssl package (3.5.6-1~deb13u2, pulled in via ca-certificates) and the fips variants ship the dhi pkg-openssl 3.5.7 rebuild; the analysis is identical for both.

CVE-2024-26461 is a memory leak in lib/gssapi/krb5/k5sealv3.c, on an error path that upstream notes cannot be triggered through GSSAPI API calls with attacker input. datahub-ingestion uses GSSAPI purely as a client when a recipe enables Kerberos authentication; a remote peer cannot drive the leaking error path, and Debian marks the issue unimportant with negligible security impact and ships no fixed version for trixie. The process is a short-lived one-shot ingestion CLI, so even a triggered leak would be bounded by the process lifetime and have no security consequence.

CVE-2024-26458 is a memory leak in lib/rpc/pmap_rmt.c, the legacy SunRPC portmapper broadcast client inside libgssrpc. The image ships libgssrpc only as a dependency of the kadmin client utilities; nothing in datahub-ingestion issues portmapper broadcast RPCs. Kerberos use here is client-side GSSAPI/SASL authentication through libgssapi-krb5-2 (libsasl2-modules-gssapi-mit) against operator-configured sources, which never enters the pmap_rmt code, so an adversary has no input channel into the leaking path. Debian marks the leak unimportant with negligible security impact and ships no fixed version for trixie; the process is additionally a short-lived one-shot CLI where a bounded leak has no security effect.

CVE-2018-5709 is an integer truncation in kadmin/dbutil/dump.c (dbentry->n_key_data assigned from a 32-bit value), code that compiles into the kdb5_util KDC database dump utility shipped in Debian's krb5-kdc/krb5-admin-server packages. This image installs only the client-side Kerberos packages (krb5-user, krb5-config, libkrb5-3, libkrb5support0, libgssapi-krb5-2) needed for Kerberos-authenticated ingestion sources. Verified in the built image: no kdb5_util or any KDC/kadmin-server tooling exists on the filesystem (only client binaries such as kadmin.mit/kinit.mit are present), so the vulnerable dump code is not shipped. Debian additionally marks the issue unimportant because the dump path only ever processes the KDC's own trusted database.

CVE-2011-3389 is BEAST, the 2011 chosen-plaintext attack against CBC cipher suites in TLS 1.0. The issue is disputed by the GnuTLS maintainer and Debian has shipped no fix since 2011 (no fixed version exists). In this image libgnutls30 is dead weight: a DT_NEEDED scan of every ELF object in the built image finds exactly one consumer, librtmp.so.1, which is itself only reachable through libcurl's RTMP(S) protocol support, and no shipped component issues rtmp:// or rtmps:// transfers (zero rtmp scheme strings in the two libcurl consumers, librdkafka and the IBM DB2 clidriver GSKit library). Exploiting BEAST additionally requires an attacker who can inject adaptive chosen plaintext into a victim TLS 1.0 CBC session, a browser-style cross-origin oracle that a one-shot metadata-ingestion CLI does not provide.

CVE-2025-15224 makes curl wrongly authenticate via a locally running SSH agent when asked to do public key authentication for SCP/SFTP transfers. No component in this image performs scp:// or sftp:// transfers via libcurl: there is no curl CLI, no SSH agent runs in the container, and the only two libcurl consumers found by a DT_NEEDED scan of every ELF object (librdkafka.so.1 and the IBM DB2 clidriver GSKit library) contain zero scp or sftp scheme strings and drive HTTPS only. The vulnerable SSH authentication path is never entered. No fixed version exists for trixie.

CVE-2025-15079 makes libcurl accept SSH hosts from the SSH library's global known_hosts file even when a transfer-specific known_hosts file is set, during SCP/SFTP transfers. No component in this image performs scp:// or sftp:// transfers via libcurl: the image has no curl CLI, and the only two libcurl consumers found by a DT_NEEDED scan of every ELF object (librdkafka.so.1 and the IBM DB2 clidriver GSKit library) contain zero scp or sftp scheme strings and drive HTTPS only. The vulnerable SSH transfer setup is therefore never entered; the advisory also describes the libssh global known_hosts behavior while Debian builds libcurl against libssh2. No fixed version exists for trixie.

CVE-2025-14017 leaks TLS option changes between concurrent multi-threaded LDAPS transfers in libcurl. The image ships no curl CLI (only libcurl4t64 as a library dependency), and a DT_NEEDED scan of every ELF object in the built image finds exactly two libcurl consumers: librdkafka.so.1 (uses libcurl solely for HTTPS OIDC token retrieval; the binary contains zero ldap scheme strings) and the IBM DB2 clidriver GSKit library bundled in site-packages (certificate and revocation handling). Neither performs LDAPS transfers through libcurl, let alone the vulnerable pattern of concurrent multi-threaded LDAPS transfers that mutate per-transfer TLS options; datahub's LDAP ingestion source uses the pure-Python python-ldap stack via libldap2, which does not route through libcurl. No fixed version exists for trixie.

CVE-2025-10966 is a missing host-verification flaw in curl's wolfSSH-powered SFTP backend. Debian does not build curl against wolfSSH: verified in the built image that libcurl.so.4.8.0 contains zero wolfssh references while libssh2 references are present (the SSH backend is libssh2), so the vulnerable wolfSSH code is not compiled into the shipped library. This matches the central Debian assessment that the wolfSSH code is not used in Debian.

GHSA-537c-gmf6-5ccf (CVE-2026-34180) is a heap buffer over-read in the OpenSSL copy bundled inside cryptography wheels when decoding crafted ASN.1 DER inputs larger than 2 GiB via d2i_X509(), d2i_PKCS7(), or related d2i_* entry points. The datahub-ingestion image uses cryptography only as a TLS client library for ingestion connectors (Snowflake, database sources, REST APIs) connecting to operator-configured endpoints; TLS handshake certificate chains and related ASN.1 objects are bounded well below 2 GiB, so an adversary cannot supply the pathological multi-gigabyte DER blob the flaw requires. A patched wheel requires cryptography>=48.0.1, but acryl-datahub 1.5.0.7 declares cryptography<47.0.0,>=46.0.5 on the snowflake and related extras in the slim install set, blocking an in-image bump until upstream lifts that cap.

The black package is not actually installed in the datahub-ingestion image. The black entry in the SBOM is a false positive sourced from the acryl_great_expectations 0.15.50.1 METADATA file, which lists 'black[jupyter]==22.3.0' as a test-only extra (Requires-Dist: black[jupyter]==22.3.0; extra == "test"). The runtime install does not request the test extra, so no black files exist on disk and no Python module 'black' is importable. The path-traversal vulnerability requires invoking the black CLI; that code path is unreachable.

The black package is not actually installed in the datahub-ingestion image: the SBOM entry is a false positive sourced from the acryl_great_expectations 0.15.50.1 METADATA file, which lists 'black[jupyter]==22.3.0' only behind the test and dev extras (Requires-Dist: black[jupyter]==22.3.0; extra == "test"), which the runtime install never requests. Verified in the built image: no black module or dist-info exists in site-packages and `python -c "import black"` fails with ModuleNotFoundError, so the vulnerable code is not present.

False positive. CVE-2026-22184 affects the untgz utility that is part of zlib source code, but Debian zlib packages (zlib1g and zlib1g-dev) do not ship the untgz utility by default. For Debian Trixie (and other versions), zlib comes from zlib1g (binaries) and does not include the untgz binary. The vulnerability scanner incorrectly flags zlib packages as vulnerable when the untgz utility is not actually present in the installed packages.
